input.content: You are an independent PLC verification engineer. Return ONLY a JSON list of test cases.

You are an independent PLC test engineer. Generate comprehensive unit test cases for the specified PLC function block.
CODESYS Simulation Timing & Edge Rules:
- dt_ms advances elapsed PLC scan time for that step; TON/TOF timers accumulate dt_ms across consecutive steps while IN keeps its active state (e.g., IN=TRUE for TON).
- Rising-edge detection (R_TRIG or x AND NOT prev_x) requires a step with x=FALSE before the step with x=TRUE.

Return a JSON array of test case objects. Each test case must have:
- id: string identifier (e.g. 'case_1')
- steps: array of steps, where each step has:
    - inputs: dictionary of input variable names and values
    - expected: dictionary of expected output variable names and values
    - dt_ms: (optional) cycle elapsed time in milliseconds

TASK SPECIFICATIONS:
{
  "id": "PUB012",
  "title": "Slab Thickness Alarm and Fault History",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "requirements": "# Slab Thickness Alarm and Fault History\n\n- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)\n\n## Requirements\n\nMonitor slab-thickness faults on a stone-cutting line, including minimum alarm holding, fault counting, normal-cutting runtime accumulation and a history of the five most recent faults.\n\n1. When THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is TRUE, THICKNESS_FAULT indicates that thickness deviation exceeds tolerance. Activate THICKNESS_ALARM immediately when the fault becomes TRUE, and hold each triggered alarm for at least 500 ms. Keep the alarm active while the fault persists.\n2. On each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of a valid fault signal, increment Slab_Fault_Counter and store the current FaultTimestamp in element 0 of Slab_Fault_History. Shift older entries toward higher indices, retaining only the five most recent entries.\n3. Accumulate Slab_Runtime_Accumulator using CycleTime only while CUTTING_RUN is TRUE, the thickness signal is valid and no thickness fault is present. Otherwise preserve the accumulated value.\n4. At power-up or whenever THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is FALSE, switch off the alarm and clear its holding state. Do not add fault records or accumulate normal runtime while the signal is invalid.\n5. At power-up, initialize the fault count, accumulated runtime and all five history entries to zero. Statistics and history are for observation and maintenance only; they must not alter the cutting equipment's operating permissive, and external callers must not modify history entries.\n\n## Interface Definition\n\n| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Input | `THICKNESS_FAULT` | `BOOL` | Thickness deviation exceeds the permitted tolerance. |\n| Input | `THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID` | `BOOL` | Thickness-signal validity; FALSE means the signal is lost or unavailable. |\n| Input | `CUTTING_RUN` | `BOOL` | Actual cutting-equipment running status. |\n| Input | `FaultTimestamp` | `DINT` | Current timestamp in seconds, used as the fault-record identifier. |\n| Input | `CycleTime` | `TIME` | Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive. |\n| Output | `THICKNESS_ALARM` | `BOOL` | Thickness alarm with a minimum 500 ms hold duration. |\n| Output | `Slab_Fault_Counter` | `UINT` | Number of valid thickness-fault occurrences. |\n| Output | `Slab_Runtime_Accumulator` | `LTIME` | Accumulated normal-cutting runtime. |\n| Output | `Slab_Fault_History` | `ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT` | Five most recent fault timestamps; index 0 is newest; read-only to callers. |",
  "scenario": "Thickness monitoring records faults, alarm minimum holding, normal-cutting time and bounded history.",
  "interface": [
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "THICKNESS_FAULT",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Thickness deviation exceeds the permitted tolerance."
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Thickness-signal validity; FALSE means the signal is lost or unavailable."
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "CUTTING_RUN",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Actual cutting-equipment running status."
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "FaultTimestamp",
      "type": "DINT",
      "description": "Current timestamp in seconds, used as the fault-record identifier."
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "CycleTime",
      "type": "TIME",
      "description": "Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive."
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "THICKNESS_ALARM",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Thickness alarm with a minimum 500 ms hold duration."
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "Slab_Fault_Counter",
      "type": "UINT",
      "description": "Number of valid thickness-fault occurrences."
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "Slab_Runtime_Accumulator",
      "type": "LTIME",
      "description": "Accumulated normal-cutting runtime."
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "Slab_Fault_History",
      "type": "ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT",
      "description": "Five most recent fault timestamps; index 0 is newest; read-only to callers."
    }
  ],
  "initial_conditions": {
    "THICKNESS_ALARM": false,
    "Slab_Fault_Counter": 0,
    "Slab_Runtime_Accumulator": "LTIME#0ns",
    "Slab_Fault_History": [
      0,
      0,
      0,
      0,
      0
    ]
  },
  "scan_semantics": "Inputs I[k] are sampled at invocation; outputs O[k] are observed after the call. Retained pre-state q[k] becomes q[k+1]. Each test resets the instance. A transition affects the same observed scan. dt_ms is elapsed time since the preceding invocation; the first invocation starts IEC timers at elapsed zero. CycleTime inputs, where supplied, are attributed to the current invocation rather than inferred from dt_ms.",
  "safety_priority": [
    "Invalid signal overrides minimum alarm holding.",
    "A persistent valid fault keeps the alarm on.",
    "Statistics never control cutting permissives."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The counted signal is valid AND fault; a valid fault after signal loss is a new occurrence.",
    "Hold starts at elapsed zero on the trigger call and releases at 500ms if the fault is absent. A fresh rising trigger restarts the hold.",
    "Invalid input cancels the hold immediately.",
    "Positive CycleTime is added on every current qualifying call, including a normal first invocation.",
    "UINT/LTIME overflow is outside these bounded cases and requires a separate policy.",
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values.",
    "On timed benchmark tests, CycleTime equals dt_ms and uses exact integer nanoseconds within 32-bit unsigned TIME bounds. FaultTimestamp is a 32-bit signed DINT (-2147483648..2147483647).",
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values."
  ],
  "atomic_propositions": {
    "valid": "THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID",
    "fault": "THICKNESS_FAULT",
    "alarm": "THICKNESS_ALARM",
    "rise": "valid AND fault AND NOT previous(valid AND fault)",
    "record": "count=pre-count+1; history[0]=FaultTimestamp; history[j]=pre-history[j-1] for j=1..4",
    "same_stats": "count and history equal pre-scan values",
    "hold": "Internal hold timer active (<500ms since last valid rising fault edge) while THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is TRUE.",
    "normal": "valid AND NOT fault AND CUTTING_RUN",
    "add": "runtime=pre-runtime+CycleTime",
    "same_time": "runtime=pre-runtime",
    "THICKNESS_FAULT": "I[k].THICKNESS_FAULT: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID": "I[k].THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "CUTTING_RUN": "I[k].CUTTING_RUN: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "FaultTimestamp": "I[k].FaultTimestamp: sampled input (DINT).",
    "CycleTime": "I[k].CycleTime: sampled input (TIME).",
    "THICKNESS_ALARM": "O[k].THICKNESS_ALARM: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "Slab_Fault_Counter": "O[k].Slab_Fault_Counter: independently observed post-scan candidate value (UINT); never defined as expected output.",
    "Slab_Runtime_Accumulator": "O[k].Slab_Runtime_Accumulator: independently observed post-scan candidate value (LTIME); never defined as expected output.",
    "Slab_Fault_History": "O[k].Slab_Fault_History: independently observed post-scan candidate value (ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT); never defined as expected output.",
    "count": "O[k].Slab_Fault_Counter",
    "history": "O[k].Slab_Fault_History",
    "runtime": "O[k].Slab_Runtime_Accumulator",
    "timing": "Internal hold start Sref.timed_contract.since records the most recent valid THICKNESS_FAULT rising-edge timestamp; a fresh rising edge during an active 500ms hold restarts the 500ms timer. Invalid input clears hold immediately.",
    "init": "At the separate pre-invocation initial observation before scan k=0: O_init.THICKNESS_ALARM=false, O_init.Slab_Fault_Counter=0, O_init.Slab_Runtime_Accumulator=\"LTIME#0ns\", O_init.Slab_Fault_History=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]."
  },
  "ltl": [
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P_init",
      "kind": "safety",
      "formula": "init",
      "description": "Before the first scan invocation, all declared OUTPUT variables and initial instance state hold their declared initial values.",
      "explanation": "Applies strictly to the fresh pre-invocation initial instance observation before scan k=0 (INITIAL_INSTANCE scope).",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "INITIAL_INSTANCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P1",
      "name": "Signal loss",
      "formula": "G(!valid -> !alarm)",
      "explanation": "Invalid signal cancels alarm immediately.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P2",
      "name": "Fault hold",
      "formula": "G(valid & (fault | hold) -> alarm)",
      "explanation": "The alarm persists during fault and hold.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P3",
      "name": "Occurrence",
      "formula": "G(rise -> record)",
      "explanation": "Each valid rising fault shifts the bounded history.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P4",
      "name": "No spurious record",
      "formula": "G(!rise -> same_stats)",
      "explanation": "Held faults and invalid inputs do not create records.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P5",
      "name": "Runtime",
      "formula": "G((normal -> add) & (!normal -> same_time))",
      "explanation": "Normal runtime counts only eligible intervals.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P6",
      "name": "Release",
      "formula": "G(valid & !fault & !hold -> !alarm)",
      "explanation": "Alarm releases when neither fault nor hold remains.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    }
  ]
}
Output budget: at most 2 cases, at most 8 steps per case. Use compact JSON. Cover a complete normal path and one important boundary. Keep reasoning concise enough to finish the entire JSON within the output budget.
